title: A Portrait of the Author as a Learning Junkie
coreMove: Reprice a postponed skill by defining the first honest competence threshold instead of measuring the first hour against mastery.
sourcePressure: The source opens on overloaded modern life, challenges the misuse of a 10,000-hour mastery benchmark, and separates practical competence from elite performance while naming early frustration as the reason many learners quit.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the chapter as a promise that twenty hours creates expertise instead of a scope correction for usable entry-level competence.

sourceAnchors.name: 10,000-hour benchmark
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support says the opening chapter questions whether it really takes 10,000 hours to become good at something and distinguishes expert performance from basic practical competence
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The 10,000-hour number can make a Tuesday evening practice session feel as if it has already failed a championship standard.

sourceAnchors.name: first twenty hours
sourceAnchors.detail: the source positions the method around moving from knowing almost nothing to performing noticeably well through a focused early practice commitment
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The first twenty hours are not a trophy; they are the bridge from helpless to useful.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital triage nurse learning basic medical Spanish for intake
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader with a high-value skill postponed because fluency feels impossible
exampleSpecs.stakes: Spanish-speaking patients wait while questions pass through a coworker
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah circles five intake questions on a laminated shift card and decides that clear pain-location questions will count as the first competence line
exampleSpecs.firstImage: alcohol wipes drying beside a laminated intake card

exampleSpecs.domain: small-town baker learning enough bookkeeping to catch cash leaks
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader avoiding numbers because accounting expertise feels too large
exampleSpecs.stakes: weekly ingredient costs are rising and nobody can explain the margin drop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lukas stops pricing himself against a certified accountant and marks one threshold: reconcile flour invoices against Friday deposits without help
exampleSpecs.firstImage: flour-dusted invoices clipped under a brass till key

exampleSpecs.domain: museum docent learning basic sign language greetings
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who wants inclusion without pretending instant fluency
exampleSpecs.stakes: a deaf school group arrives next month and the museum has no interpreter for the welcome station
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille asks a local tutor to test whether she can greet, point to the map, and explain the coatroom before adding any new signs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded gallery map held between two nervous hands

exampleSpecs.domain: community radio host learning audio editing basics
exampleSpecs.audience: a creator stuck because professional production standards make starting look absurd
exampleSpecs.stakes: a local interview sits unreleased because the raw file has two long mistakes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James predicts he needs full production training, then proves the useful threshold by cutting one cough, one dead pause, and exporting a clean two-minute segment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red waveform spike beside a sticky note that says cough

exampleSpecs.domain: park volunteer learning basic chainsaw safety vocabulary without operating the saw
exampleSpecs.audience: a cautious reader who needs bounded competence around a risky tool
exampleSpecs.stakes: storm cleanup briefings are confusing and unsafe when she cannot name parts or hazards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anke writes her threshold as identifying chain brake, kickback zone, and stop command during safety briefing, not cutting wood herself
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange safety chaps hanging from a wet park-service hook

exampleSpecs.domain: Toronto apartment gardener learning seed-starting for one balcony crop
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose hobby remains imaginary because expert growers look unreachable
exampleSpecs.stakes: her spring seedlings die every year before the first transplant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya defines competence as getting six basil seedlings from tray to balcony planter, then removes every advanced gardening goal from the first month
exampleSpecs.firstImage: condensation on a clear seed-tray lid above six labeled cells
